architecture_change_requests.decision_rationale: The landing zone already carries the controls the product needs, and the on-premises estate has no capacity plan that reaches the launch date.
architecture_change_requests.description: Whether the new product goes onto the AWS landing zone or onto the existing on-premises estate the card systems run on.
architecture_change_requests.impact_assessment: Eight new systems, none of them replacing anything live. The ledger, the bureau and the CRM gain a caller through the integration hub rather than changing.
architecture_change_requests.name: Build installment lending on AWS rather than on-premises
architecture_change_requests.principle_alignment: Buy the platform, build the differentiator.

architecture_change_requests.decision_rationale: The list management is the product, and maintaining it in-house would be a permanent obligation for a capability that is not a differentiator.
architecture_change_requests.description: Whether to extend the fraud platform with sanctions and adverse-media screening or to onboard a vendor product for it.
architecture_change_requests.impact_assessment: A vendor tenant outside the estate, reached through a private egress path, and one live system changed: the authorization switch becomes its caller.
architecture_change_requests.name: Buy sanctions screening rather than build it
architecture_change_requests.principle_alignment: Buy the platform, build the differentiator.

architecture_change_requests.decision_rationale: Deferred until the lending product has run a full cycle. Consolidating a Restricted store into a system that has not yet been through a release would move the risk rather than remove it.
architecture_change_requests.description: Whether the card servicing operational datastore should be retired into the new lending database once lending is live, rather than run as a second operational store for the same customers.
architecture_change_requests.impact_assessment: Would retire one live system and change one that is not built yet. Until it is taken, the datastore stays as it is: High criticality, Restricted, and recording no control of its own.
architecture_change_requests.name: Fold the card servicing datastore into the lending database
architecture_change_requests.principle_alignment: One system of record per kind of data.

architecture_change_requests.decision_rationale: Liveness detection is a model the vendor retrains against fraud patterns we never see; building it would be a permanent obligation for a capability that is not a differentiator.
architecture_change_requests.description: Whether to extend the identity service with document capture and liveness checking or to onboard a vendor for it.
architecture_change_requests.impact_assessment: A vendor tenancy outside the estate, reached over a private path, and one live system changed: the identity service sends the capture and acts on the callback.
architecture_change_requests.name: Buy identity document verification rather than build it
architecture_change_requests.principle_alignment: Buy the platform, build the differentiator.

architecture_change_requests.decision_rationale: The shape exists to make a new cardholder product a handful of answers rather than a build, and it had never been used. A product that adds one part to it is the test the shape needs, and redemption is the product whose failure costs least while it is proven.
architecture_change_requests.description: Whether to add redemption to the card servicing product or to build it as its own product on the Azure digital shape, the first to sit on it.
architecture_change_requests.impact_assessment: Five new systems on the Azure landing zone and nothing live changed. One shared service added to the landing zone -- Event Hubs, the event stream the worker consumes -- which every later Azure product with a worker inherits. The proposed rewards ledger stays the source of balances.
architecture_change_requests.name: Build rewards redemption on the Azure product shape
architecture_change_requests.principle_alignment: Build on the shape; let the landing zone answer for the parts.

architecture_change_requests.decision_rationale: A shape is worth naming when the second product like it arrives. The first merchant product uses the same parts as the Azure digital shape plus a role, and the library already makes those parts a handful of answers; a shape for a product of one would be a file nobody reuses.
architecture_change_requests.description: Whether a merchant-facing product needs a shape of its own before it is built, or can be assembled from the parts the digital shapes share and earn a shape when a second one follows.
architecture_change_requests.impact_assessment: Four new systems on the Azure landing zone, one new actor, and nothing live changed. The compose block is the record of what was chosen; if a second merchant product is assembled from it, it is promoted to a shape.
architecture_change_requests.name: Assemble the merchant portal from parts rather than a shape
architecture_change_requests.principle_alignment: Assemble from the library; name the shape when it repeats.

architecture_change_requests.decision_rationale: The dealer platforms that start a point-of-sale application already integrate through Apigee on Google Cloud, and the shortest private path to them is to land beside them. The library made the cost small: the digital shape's parts are the same on every cloud, so the new shape is a provider line and the bindings, and the landing zone is the same kinds of service the AWS and Azure zones carry.
architecture_change_requests.description: Whether a third cloud is worth a landing zone of its own for one product, or the product should land on Azure beside the other digital products and reach its dealer partners over the internet.
architecture_change_requests.impact_assessment: A Google Cloud landing zone of nineteen services, a third digital shape, four new systems and one data asset; nothing live changed. The zone's kinds are the same as the other two, so every block resolves; the first `library.landing_zone_gap` warning, if one appears, names what the zone still lacks.
architecture_change_requests.name: Land the first product on Google Cloud
architecture_change_requests.principle_alignment: Same parts, different bindings; land beside the partner, not across the internet from it.

architecture_change_requests.decision_rationale: A checkout decision has seconds, and bureau data says what was borrowed, not what is affordable this month. Open banking data, with the shopper's consent, answers the question the regulator asks in the time the sale allows. Bought, because the open banking connections and the categorization are a vendor's whole business and nobody's here.
architecture_change_requests.description: Whether point-of-sale finance assesses affordability from the shopper's own bank data, bought from an open banking vendor, or from the bureau data the installment lending product already uses.
architecture_change_requests.impact_assessment: One vendor tenancy, a gateway, a private egress and a webhook listener in the lending project on Google Cloud, feeding the point-of-sale API. Restricted data from the first byte, so the path is private and the vendor's retention is contractual. The first bought capability on the Google Cloud side; the vendor shape needed a provider line and nothing else.
architecture_change_requests.name: Buy affordability data on open banking rails
architecture_change_requests.principle_alignment: Buy what is a vendor's whole business; land beside the caller; keep restricted data off the public path.

architecture_change_requests.decision_rationale: The data is born on Google Cloud and the analysts who want it sit with the product; carrying it to Snowflake for a nightly curation would cross clouds twice, and pay egress both ways, for a dataset nobody on the Azure side reads. Collibra registers it either way, so governance does not move with the warehouse.
architecture_change_requests.description: Whether point-of-sale finance's performance data is curated in BigQuery beside the product, or carried to the enterprise warehouse on the Azure side the way every other data product is.
architecture_change_requests.impact_assessment: A second workload project on the Google Cloud hub, four landing-zone services the zone did not list -- BigQuery, Dataflow, Cloud Composer, Looker -- and the first data product shape with a Google binding. The enterprise warehouse gains nothing and loses nothing; the catalog gains a dataset on a second cloud.
architecture_change_requests.name: Curate Google Cloud data on Google Cloud
architecture_change_requests.principle_alignment: Curate data where it is born; one catalog whichever cloud; land beside the caller.

frameworks.description: The Banking Industry Architecture Network's service landscape. A reference model of banking service domains, organized into business areas. Strong on what a bank does and deliberately silent on how it is run.
frameworks.name: BIAN
frameworks.scope: Banking business capabilities and service domains

frameworks.description: A cross-industry process taxonomy. Used here for the enabling tier, where a card-specific name adds nothing: finance, HR and corporate services look much the same in any industry, and inventing local names for them costs comparability for no benefit.
frameworks.name: APQC Process Classification Framework

frameworks.description: Service management practice: incident, change, problem, service level. The frame technology operations is actually run and audited against, and the vocabulary a service management tool already speaks.
frameworks.name: ITIL 4

frameworks.description: The data management body of knowledge: governance, quality, architecture, metadata, master data, security. The only one of these with a defensible account of what a data function is responsible for.
frameworks.name: DAMA-DMBOK

frameworks.description: Governance and management objectives for enterprise IT. Where ITIL says how to run a service, this says how to know whether it is being run well, which is why the risk and technology governance domains answer to it.
frameworks.name: COBIT 2019
frameworks.scope: Governance and management of enterprise IT

frameworks.description: Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover. The five functions most security programs are structured and reported against, and the one framing a board recognizes.
frameworks.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework

frameworks.description: The certifiable information security management standard. Named separately from the NIST framework because certification is a fact about the organization and a practice framework is not.
frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 27001

frameworks.description: The card industry's data security standard. Not a framework anybody chose: it is a condition of processing card transactions, which is why it governs the payment and merchant domains whatever anyone thinks of it.
frameworks.name: PCI DSS

frameworks.description: The Business Architecture Guild's body of knowledge. Governs how the capability map and the value streams are built rather than what is in them, which makes it the framework this repository's own business layer answers to.
frameworks.name: BIZBOK

frameworks.description: The architecture development method and content metamodel this repository's entity types are drawn from. It governs the practice of architecture, not any business domain, which is why nothing but the architecture function maps to it.
frameworks.name: TOGAF

frameworks.description: The Cyber Risk Institute's Profile: the financial sector's harmonization of NIST CSF, ISO 27001 and the regulators' expectations into one set of diagnostic statements. What a bank is examined against for cyber, and therefore what the security domain is governed by rather than informed by.
frameworks.name: CRI Profile
frameworks.scope: Cyber risk management and resilience in financial institutions

processes.description: Build, package, scan, and promote a change through environments automatically, with gates that stop a failing build.
processes.name: Run the build and deployment pipeline

processes.description: Run static, dependency, and secret scanning on every change and remediate findings within the applicable service level.
processes.name: Scan code and dependencies for security defects

processes.description: Record, size, and prioritize technical debt, and reserve capacity in each increment to retire it. Debt items live in the same backlog as features so the trade-off is visible at prioritization, not discovered at incident time.
processes.name: Manage technical debt

processes.description: Control configuration and feature-flag changes so behavior can be changed or reverted without a code release, with an audit trail.
processes.name: Manage application configuration and feature flags

processes.description: Diagnose and fix application defects escalated from service management, and feed root causes back into the backlog.
processes.name: Support a production application

processes.description: Retire an application: migrate or archive its data to the retention schedule, remove interfaces and access, and update the inventory.
processes.name: Decommission an application

processes.description: Accept a cardholder payment through any channel and apply it to the account on the correct effective date.
processes.name: Capture and apply cardholder payment

processes.description: Segment delinquent accounts and assign the contact and treatment strategy. Runs nightly after delinquency bucketing; the strategy drives queue, channel, intensity, and hardship routing, and a wrong assignment is a conduct risk as much as a loss risk.
processes.name: Assign delinquency treatment strategy

processes.description: Execute outbound contact attempts within contact-frequency and communication constraints. Contact windows, frequency caps, and channel consent come from FDCPA, Reg F, and TCPA; the process starts at queue release and ends when the disposition is recorded.
processes.name: Execute outbound collections contact

processes.description: Agree, document, and administer a payment arrangement or settlement. Covers promises to pay, long-term arrangements, and settlements; terms must fit the approved matrix, and the arrangement drives bucket movement and interest treatment downstream.
processes.name: Negotiate and administer payment arrangement

processes.description: Execute charge-off on policy timing and record the accounting effect. Timing follows the charge-off policy aligned to regulatory guidance; the entry moves the balance to charged-off status and hands the account to recovery placement.
processes.name: Execute charge-off

processes.description: Compile and furnish account data to the consumer reporting agencies. Monthly Metro 2 furnishing to the bureaus; accuracy is an FCRA obligation, and the file must reconcile to the system of record before transmission.
processes.name: Furnish credit bureau data

processes.description: Investigate and respond to a consumer credit reporting dispute within the required period. Direct and bureau-routed disputes both land here; FCRA sets the investigation window, and the outcome must correct both the bureau file and the account when the consumer is right.
processes.name: Handle credit reporting dispute

processes.description: Generate and deliver the required validation notice within the prescribed period. The validation notice is a statutory precondition to continued collection on affected accounts; timing and content mistakes surface directly as regulatory findings.
processes.name: Issue debt validation notice

processes.description: Detect a regulatory change, assess applicability and impact, and drive implementation. Starts at horizon scanning and ends when the change is implemented and evidenced in the affected processes; applicability calls are documented even when the answer is not applicable.
processes.name: Assess and land regulatory change

processes.description: Execute a scheduled control test and record the result and any exceptions. Runs the monitoring schedule agreed with the compliance plan; exceptions become issues in remediation tracking with owners and dates rather than emails.
processes.name: Execute compliance monitoring test

processes.description: Screen parties and transactions against sanctions and watchlists and adjudicate hits. Screening runs at onboarding and on list updates across cardholders, clients, and suppliers; a hit blocks processing until dispositioned, and the disposition is retained as evidence.
processes.name: Screen for sanctions and watchlists

processes.description: Investigate an alert and, where warranted, prepare and file the regulatory report. The SAR decision and filing run on the BSA clock from alert qualification; the investigation file must stand on its own for examiner review, and filing is confidential by law.
processes.name: Investigate and file suspicious activity report

processes.description: Aggregate and analyze complaint data for unfair or deceptive practice risk. Feeds the UDAAP program: complaint taxonomy, root cause, and trend analysis across channels, including complaints held by servicing clients about serviced portfolios.
processes.name: Analyze complaint signal for conduct risk

processes.description: Define, test, approve, and deploy changes to the credit decision strategy and its cutoffs. Strategy changes ship through champion-challenger testing with documented approval; the deployed strategy is the single decisioning authority for originations.
processes.name: Set and deploy credit decision strategy

processes.description: Build, document, and validate credit and fraud models prior to production deployment. Development evidence, data lineage, and validation results follow model risk management expectations; nothing reaches production without an independent validation record.
processes.name: Develop and validate credit model

processes.description: Identify eligible accounts and execute line increases under the approved strategy. Eligibility, ability-to-pay checks, and notice requirements are built into the program design; execution is batch with opt-out handling.
processes.name: Execute credit line increase program

processes.description: Apply risk-driven line decreases or account actions, with required notice. Adverse action obligations apply to decreases and closures just as they do to declines; the notice must state the principal reasons and bureau information used.
processes.name: Execute credit line decrease or account action

processes.description: Review vintage, roll-rate, and segment performance against risk appetite and record the actions agreed at the portfolio credit review.
processes.name: Conduct monthly portfolio credit review

processes.description: Produce the credit loss forecast and set the allowance for the reporting period. The CECL forecast and allowance feed the financial statements; assumptions, overlays, and approvals are documented for both auditors and examiners.
processes.name: Produce loss forecast and allowance

processes.description: Define and deploy the rules governing real-time authorization decisions. Authorization strategy balances approval rates, fraud losses, and credit exposure in real time; changes deploy through the same testing discipline as origination strategy.
processes.name: Maintain authorization strategy

processes.description: Review account risk periodically and decide reissue, close, or continue. Periodic account review drives reissue, line, and closure decisions at card expiry and on risk triggers; decisions carry the same notice obligations as any adverse action.
processes.name: Perform account review and reissue decision

processes.description: Source consumer bureau data for prescreen, account review, and portfolio monitoring under permissible purpose, and manage refresh cadence and quality.
processes.name: Acquire and refresh credit bureau data

processes.description: Receive, understand, and resolve a cardholder inquiry across any servicing channel. First-contact resolution is the design goal across phone, chat, and secure message; anything unresolved routes to a case with ownership and a promise date.
processes.name: Handle cardholder inquiry

processes.description: Acquire, integrate, and land source data into the enterprise data platform. Ingestion lands source extracts into the platform with schema validation, lineage capture, and quality checks at the gate rather than downstream.
processes.name: Ingest and integrate source data

processes.description: Deploy an approved model to production and monitor its ongoing performance. Deployment follows model risk approval; monitoring covers drift, stability, and performance against the validation baseline, with retirement triggers agreed up front.
processes.name: Deploy and monitor production model

processes.description: Register a data asset, assign ownership, and classify it for handling. Onboarding assigns owner, steward, classification, and retention up front; the Collibra registration is the system of record this model's stub points at.
processes.name: Onboard and classify data asset

processes.description: Measure data quality against defined expectations and drive remediation. Quality rules run against critical data elements with published thresholds; breaches create remediation work with the data owner, not just a dashboard entry.
processes.name: Measure and remediate data quality

processes.description: Publish metadata, lineage, and ownership into the governance catalog. The catalog is where consumers discover data and its lineage; publication is part of change delivery, not an afterthought, so the catalog stays current by construction.
processes.name: Publish metadata and lineage to catalog

processes.description: Apply the retention schedule and execute defensible disposition of records. Disposition is defensible destruction: eligibility verified against holds, execution evidenced by certificate, and the retention schedule is the single authority.
processes.name: Execute records retention and disposition

processes.description: Identify accounts that have missed a payment and assign them to the correct delinquency bucket. Bucketing runs in the nightly cycle and is the trigger for every downstream collections treatment; a bucketing error propagates into contact, reporting, and accounting.
processes.name: Detect and bucket delinquent account

processes.description: Register and authenticate a cardholder for web and mobile self-service. Enrollment binds the cardholder to a verified identity with step-up options; weak enrollment is the account-takeover front door, so identity proofing follows the fraud strategy.
processes.name: Enroll cardholder in digital servicing

processes.description: Execute a cardholder self-service action in web or mobile without agent involvement. Self-service actions execute against the same core services as agent actions, with the same entitlements; the channel changes, the control does not.
processes.name: Serve digital self-service transaction

processes.description: Take a cardholder dispute claim, apply provisional credit, investigate, determine, and notify within regulatory timers.
processes.name: Process cardholder dispute claim

processes.description: Submit and track a chargeback through the network within the applicable filing window. Chargeback rights and filing windows differ by network and reason code; a missed window converts a recoverable dispute into an issuer loss.
processes.name: Execute network chargeback

processes.description: Evaluate merchant representment and pursue pre-arbitration where warranted. Representment evidence is weighed against the reason code requirements; pre-arbitration is pursued only where the economics and the evidence support it.
processes.name: Process representment and pre-arbitration

processes.description: Make the final dispute determination, adjust the account, and issue the compliant notice. The determination closes the Reg E or Reg Z clock: account adjustment, provisional credit disposition, and the written explanation must all land within the window.
processes.name: Finalize dispute determination and notify

processes.description: Define and refresh the target state for each domain and the sequenced roadmap to reach it, aligned to the investment plan.
processes.name: Maintain target-state architecture and roadmap

processes.description: Assess a proposed solution against standards, target state, and risk before funding and again before build; record the decision.
processes.name: Review solution architecture for an initiative

processes.description: Evaluate a request to deviate from a standard, set conditions and expiry, and track the exception to closure.
processes.name: Grant or decline an architecture exception

processes.description: Author, review, version, and retire the standards and reference models that solution reviews are judged against.
processes.name: Maintain architecture standards and reference models

processes.description: Rate each application and platform for tolerate, invest, migrate, or eliminate; identify duplication and end-of-support exposure.
processes.name: Assess technology lifecycle and rationalization

processes.description: Keep the business architecture model current: harvest changes, run the quality gates, and publish the refreshed model to its consumers.
processes.name: Maintain the capability map and process inventory

processes.description: Trace a proposed system or interface change to the processes, capabilities, and clients it affects, and brief the change authority.
processes.name: Assess change impact of a proposed system change

processes.description: Run the evaluation for a new technology or vendor platform: requirements, options, proof of concept, and a recommendation into procurement.
processes.name: Evaluate and select a technology or platform

processes.description: Keep the inventory of applications, platforms, and interfaces complete and attributed, including owner, tier, hosting, and lifecycle state.
processes.name: Maintain the application and technology inventory

processes.description: Calculate and recognize interchange, fee, and servicing revenue for the period. Revenue recognition follows the network and client contract terms; interchange, fees, and servicing revenue post to the ledger with support for audit.
processes.name: Recognize interchange and servicing revenue

processes.description: Validate, approve, and execute payment to a supplier. Invoices match to contract and receipt before payment; approval limits and segregation of duties are the fraud controls the audit tests.
processes.name: Process supplier payment

processes.description: Detect a suspected fraudulent transaction, action the alert, and contact the cardholder. Alert handling runs against loss and customer-friction budgets; actions span block, reissue, and contact, and the clock matters because exposure grows per transaction.
processes.name: Detect and action transaction fraud alert

processes.description: Investigate a suspected fraud case and reach a documented determination. The case determination separates true fraud from friendly fraud and abuse, drives the Reg E liability decision, and feeds the loss and strategy data.
processes.name: Investigate and adjudicate fraud case

processes.description: Contain, remediate, and communicate an account takeover or identity compromise event. Account takeover response contains first, then remediates credentials, reverses fraudulent activity, and communicates with the cardholder; speed limits the loss.
processes.name: Respond to account takeover event

processes.description: Pursue recovery of fraud losses and write off the residual with correct accounting. Recovery pursues merchants, networks, and other issuers where rights exist; the residual writes off to the fraud loss line with the accounting evidenced.
processes.name: Recover and write off fraud loss

processes.description: Compile and submit fraud reporting to the networks within required thresholds. Network fraud reporting (TC40, SAFE) has thresholds and deadlines; late or wrong reporting risks network compliance programs and fines.
processes.name: Submit network fraud reporting

processes.description: Define, test, and deploy changes to fraud detection rules and models. Strategy changes are tested against recent fraud and false-positive performance before deployment; every rule change is versioned and reversible.
processes.name: Maintain fraud detection strategy

processes.description: Determine, fund, and report the daily liquidity and funding position. The daily position covers settlement obligations, deposit flows, and contingency lines; a funding miss is a same-day escalation, not a report.
processes.name: Manage daily funding position

processes.description: Complete the period-end close, including reconciliations, accruals, and reporting sign-off. The close calendar drives reconciliations, accruals, and sign-offs to the reporting deadline; open items age visibly and block sign-off past threshold.
processes.name: Execute monthly financial close

processes.description: Grant, review, and certify access to systems and data. Access follows least privilege with owner approval; the quarterly certification and automatic revocation of uncertified access are the controls CRI assesses.
processes.name: Provision and certify access

processes.description: Detect, investigate, contain, and remediate a security event. Detection through containment runs the incident playbook with severity-driven escalation; the timeline is evidence for both the CRI assessment and any notification duty.
processes.name: Detect and respond to security event

processes.description: Triage and remediate an identified vulnerability within the applicable service level. Severity sets the remediation SLA; breaches escalate rather than languish, and closure requires verification, not just a patch record.
processes.name: Remediate vulnerability

processes.description: Maintain the cardholder data environment scope and the supporting compliance evidence. PCI scope is maintained continuously: network segmentation, asset inventory, and evidence collection, so assessment is a report, not a scramble.
processes.name: Maintain cardholder data scope and evidence

processes.description: Calculate and post interchange and settlement accounting entries to the ledger. Interchange entries reconcile to network reports before posting; unexplained variances stop the post rather than flowing into revenue.
processes.name: Post interchange and settlement entries

processes.description: Source, screen, and permission prospect data for use in acquisition campaigns. Prospect data carries permissible-purpose and suppression obligations; the list that leaves this process is the compliant universe for everything downstream.
processes.name: Build and permission prospect list

processes.description: Define offer criteria and terms, and obtain compliance approval before release. A firm offer of credit commits the bank under FCRA; criteria, terms, and the compliance sign-off are locked before any channel sees the offer.
processes.name: Construct and approve firm offer of credit

processes.description: Deploy the approved offer across selected channels and manage in-flight performance. In-flight management covers channel performance, budget, and suppression hygiene; changes to a live campaign re-enter compliance review when terms move.
processes.name: Execute acquisition campaign

processes.description: Review creative, disclosures, and claims for regulatory adequacy before release. Review covers claims, disclosures, and UDAAP risk across every asset and channel; nothing ships without the documented sign-off this process exists to produce.
processes.name: Review marketing creative for compliance

processes.description: Evaluate response, approval, and early vintage economics for in-flight campaigns and decide continue, adjust, or stop.
processes.name: Review campaign performance and adjust targeting

processes.description: Reconcile network settlement files against internal transaction and ledger positions and resolve breaks.
processes.name: Reconcile network settlement

processes.description: Accept and validate a complete card application from any origination channel. Capture is complete when the application has every field decisioning needs and the applicant has the required disclosures; incomplete applications route to cure, not decline.
processes.name: Capture card application

processes.description: Verify the applicant's identity and record evidence satisfying customer identification obligations. CIP evidence is retained per BSA requirements; verification failures route to document request rather than automatic decline, and synthetic identity signals feed fraud screening.
processes.name: Verify applicant identity and satisfy CIP

processes.description: Score and adjudicate the application for synthetic, stolen, and first-party fraud risk. Fraud screening runs before credit decisioning so stolen and synthetic identities never consume a bureau pull; referred applications go to manual review with an SLA.
processes.name: Screen application for fraud

processes.description: Apply the approved credit strategy to render an approve, decline, or counter-offer decision with a line assignment.
processes.name: Execute credit decision

processes.description: Generate and deliver a compliant adverse action or counter-offer notice within the required period. ECOA and FCRA set the notice content and the clock; the principal reasons must match the actual decision factors, which is exactly what fair-lending testing checks.
processes.name: Issue adverse action notice

processes.description: Open the account on the core platform and issue the card credential. Account establishment writes the account of record and triggers credential issuance; a failure here strands an approved applicant, which is why it carries a same-day SLA.
processes.name: Establish account and issue credentials

processes.description: Oversee vendor-executed card personalization, production, and delivery, including inventory, service levels, and exception handling.
processes.name: Manage card production and fulfillment

processes.description: Provision the card credential into a digital wallet or tokenized environment. Wallet provisioning runs the network token flows with step-up verification where risk requires; weak provisioning is a known fraud vector the strategy watches.
processes.name: Provision credential to digital wallet

processes.description: Manage applications withdrawn by the applicant or abandoned before completion. Withdrawn and abandoned applications still carry notice, retention, and bureau obligations; this process closes them compliantly instead of letting them age.
processes.name: Handle application withdrawal and abandonment

processes.description: Produce contracted reporting, respond to oversight requests, and manage obligations under the issuing bank agreement.
processes.name: Fulfill issuing bank oversight obligations

processes.description: Receive, decision, and respond to a real-time authorization request within the network response window.
processes.name: Process authorization request

processes.description: Receive network clearing files and post transactions to cardholder accounts. Clearing ingestion matches presentments to authorizations, posts to accounts, and routes exceptions; the file must balance to network totals before posting completes.
processes.name: Ingest clearing file and post transactions

processes.description: Handle returned and reversed payments and assess the associated fees. Return handling reverses the payment application, restores the balance, assesses any permitted fee, and feeds NSF patterns to risk; Reg E error claims can start here.
processes.name: Process returned payment and assess NSF

processes.description: Issue, update, suspend, and delete payment tokens and credentials. Token lifecycle events flow between networks, wallets, and the account of record; a stale token strands the cardholder's wallet, so lifecycle sync is monitored.
processes.name: Manage token and credential lifecycle

processes.description: Assess and implement network mandate and release changes by the required date. Network mandates carry hard effective dates and fines for misses; assessment, build, and attestation are tracked per mandate from bulletin to production.
processes.name: Implement network mandate release

processes.description: Receive, verify, and fulfill a consumer privacy rights request within the required period. Identity verification precedes any disclosure; state privacy laws set the clocks and the evidence of fulfillment is retained per request.
processes.name: Fulfill consumer privacy request

processes.description: Define, price, and obtain approval for a change to a card product. A product change binds pricing, terms, and eligibility; approval spans product, credit, finance, legal, and compliance before configuration starts.
processes.name: Design and approve product change

processes.description: Author, review, approve, and version cardholder agreements and disclosures. Agreements and disclosures are versioned with effective dates; every account references the version it was disclosed under, which is what makes remediation tractable.
processes.name: Author and version disclosure

processes.description: Configure, test, and release a product for origination across all affected systems. Launch is a coordinated configuration across origination, core, servicing, and statements, verified in test before the product opens to volume.
processes.name: Launch product to market

processes.description: Sunset a product and migrate affected accounts with required notice. Retirement manages the migration and notices for live accounts; terms changes ride the change-in-terms rules, and the product stays resolvable for history.
processes.name: Retire or migrate product

processes.description: Decide scope, risk-based depth, environments, data, and entry and exit criteria for a release before build starts.
processes.name: Plan the test strategy for a release

processes.description: Author, review, and prune automated tests so the regression suite stays fast, trusted, and aligned to current behavior.
processes.name: Build and maintain the automated regression suite

processes.description: Run planned functional tests and the regression suite against a candidate build, and record results against the plan.
processes.name: Execute functional and regression testing

processes.description: Load, soak, and failover-test a candidate against stated capacity and recovery objectives before a material release.
processes.name: Execute performance and resilience testing

processes.description: Prepare scripts and data, run acceptance with business owners, and obtain their sign-off or documented rejection.
processes.name: Run user acceptance testing with the business

processes.description: Triage, prioritize, assign, and verify defects found in test or production, and report defect trends by area.
processes.name: Manage defects to closure

processes.description: Stand up and refresh non-production environments with representative, masked data, and retire them on schedule.
processes.name: Provision test environments and masked data

processes.description: Assess test results, open defects, and exit criteria, and issue or withhold the quality certification the change authority relies on.
processes.name: Certify a release for production

processes.description: Run post-deployment checks and smoke tests in production, confirm monitoring is green, and trigger rollback if criteria fail.
processes.name: Verify a release in production

processes.description: Select, place, and monitor charged-off accounts with an external collection agency. Agency placement follows the approved network with performance and conduct oversight; the agency acts in the bank's name, so its conduct is the bank's risk.
processes.name: Place account with collection agency

processes.description: Assemble, price, and execute a sale of charged-off receivables. Debt sale packages carry account-level data quality and documentation warranties; buyer diligence and post-sale complaint routing are part of the process, not after-thoughts.
processes.name: Execute debt sale

processes.description: Receive, verify, and action a bankruptcy notification with required account treatment. The automatic stay stops collection on notice; verification, claim filing, and account treatment follow bankruptcy chapter rules with dates that are court deadlines.
processes.name: Handle bankruptcy notification

processes.description: Verify a deceased notification and manage the account through estate resolution. Estate handling balances recovery with conduct: verified notification stops collection contact, and the claim proceeds through the estate at the estate's pace.
processes.name: Handle deceased cardholder and estate

processes.description: Post recoveries and account for proceeds from agency, legal, and sale channels. Proceeds post against charged-off balances with channel attribution; recoveries feed the loss forecast, so mis-posting distorts the allowance.
processes.name: Post recovery and account for proceeds

processes.description: Assemble, validate, and certify the data supporting regulatory reporting submissions. Report data is assembled from governed sources with reconciliation to the ledger and prior submissions; certification is a named officer's sign-off, not a batch job.
processes.name: Prepare regulatory reporting data

processes.description: Calculate and post rewards earn to the rewards ledger for qualifying activity. Earn accrues per the program terms with promotional multipliers; the accrual creates the liability finance reconciles, so earn rules and accounting stay in lockstep.
processes.name: Accrue rewards earn

processes.description: Execute a cardholder rewards redemption and settle the resulting obligation. Redemption executes across cash, statement credit, and partner channels; partner settlement follows the program contract, and failed redemptions reverse cleanly.
processes.name: Process rewards redemption

processes.description: Reconcile the rewards ledger to the recorded liability and resolve differences. The rewards liability reconciliation catches earn, redemption, and expiry drift between the ledger and finance; differences are investigated, not plugged.
processes.name: Reconcile rewards liability

processes.description: Track an identified issue through remediation to evidenced closure. Issues from any source (audit, compliance, self-identified, exam) run one lifecycle: owner, action plan, dates, and evidenced closure that survives challenge.
processes.name: Manage issue and remediation to closure

processes.description: Perform independent validation of a model and record the outcome and conditions. Independent validation is organizationally separate from development; findings condition or block production use, and revalidation triggers are set at approval.
processes.name: Validate model independently

processes.description: Coordinate the response to a regulatory examination, including evidence and findings. Exam coordination controls the single flow of requests, evidence, and meetings; every submission is logged and consistent with what other responses have said.
processes.name: Coordinate regulatory examination

processes.description: Calculate interest, fees, and the minimum payment due for the billing cycle. Cycle assessment applies the cardholder agreement exactly: interest method, fee triggers, and minimum-payment formula, because a systematic error here is a remediation event.
processes.name: Assess interest, fees, and minimum payment

processes.description: Deliver the statement by the cardholder's elected channel and retain it for retrieval. Delivery honors the e-consent election and postal fallback; the archived statement is the legal record retrieved for disputes and subpoenas.
processes.name: Deliver and archive statement

processes.description: Apply approved goodwill credits, fee reversals, and billing corrections. Adjustments carry approval limits and reason codes; patterns feed complaint and conduct analysis because repeated goodwill on the same defect is a signal.
processes.name: Process billing adjustment or goodwill credit

processes.description: Execute a cardholder-requested change to account details or preferences. Maintenance changes execute after authentication with an audit trail; address changes get extra scrutiny because they precede takeover fraud.
processes.name: Execute account maintenance request

processes.description: Authenticate a cardholder to policy before disclosing information or executing a change. Authentication strength scales with request risk; failures route to step-up rather than disclosure, and the policy is tuned with the fraud team.
processes.name: Authenticate cardholder

processes.description: Capture, classify, resolve, and evidence a cardholder complaint. Complaint handling runs intake through evidenced resolution with regulatory routing where required; the taxonomy feeds UDAAP analysis, so classification is not clerical.
processes.name: Capture and resolve complaint

processes.description: Generate and deliver a regulatory or contractual notice to the cardholder. Notice generation is driven by account events with content owned by legal and compliance; proof of delivery and version are retained per notice.
processes.name: Generate and deliver required notice

processes.description: Assess eligibility and enroll an account into a hardship or payment assistance program. Hardship enrollment applies documented eligibility consistently; program terms change interest, fees, and reporting, so enrollment is evidenced and reviewed.
processes.name: Enroll account in hardship or assistance program

processes.description: Author, review, and publish agent-facing knowledge and guidance. Knowledge content is the agent's authority in the moment; review cadence and ownership keep it aligned with policy, because stale guidance becomes wrong answers at scale.
processes.name: Maintain servicing knowledge content

processes.description: Sample, monitor, score, and calibrate servicing interactions for quality and regulatory compliance signal.
processes.name: Monitor and score servicing interactions

processes.description: Collect, hold, apply, and refund security deposits for secured card accounts, including graduation and charge-off application, with correct accounting and disclosure treatment.
processes.name: Administer secured card deposit lifecycle

processes.description: Identify covered borrowers, apply the required rate and fee protections, and evidence compliance for servicemember accounts.
processes.name: Apply servicemember and military lending protections

processes.description: Determine and fund the daily settlement position with the networks. The settlement position must fund by the network deadline in the settlement currency; a miss is a network compliance event, so the process carries same-day escalation.
processes.name: Fund daily network settlement position

processes.description: Reconcile cash and suspense account positions and clear aged items. Cash and suspense reconcile daily with aging visible; suspense is a control account, and items that age past threshold escalate to investigation.
processes.name: Reconcile cash and suspense accounts

processes.description: Investigate settlement breaks and exceptions and drive them to resolution. Settlement exceptions are worked to root cause across network reports, the gateway, and the ledger; recurring breaks feed a fix, not a workaround.
processes.name: Investigate and clear settlement exception

processes.description: Monitor interchange qualification rates, identify downgrades, and drive corrections in processing configuration.
processes.name: Monitor and optimize interchange qualification

processes.description: Cut the billing cycle and generate the cardholder statement including the rewards position. Cycle cut is the hard deadline that sequences assessment, statement generation, and delivery; a late cut cascades into payment due dates and regulatory timing.
processes.name: Cut cycle and generate statement

processes.description: Assess, diligence, price, and execute the acquisition or sale of a card portfolio, through to hand-off into conversion.
processes.name: Evaluate and execute portfolio transaction

processes.description: Design, build, test, and release a software change into production. The umbrella delivery flow from approved demand to production release; the engineering-level decomposition lives in the P-APPDEV and P-QE processes it coordinates.
processes.name: Deliver software change

processes.description: Detect, triage, resolve, and review a service incident. Incident response runs detect, triage, resolve, and review with severity-driven communication; customer-impacting incidents feed problem management and the resilience picture.
processes.name: Respond to service incident

processes.description: Plan and execute a recovery test against committed recovery objectives. The annual test exercises recovery against committed RTO and RPO with business participation; misses become tracked remediation, and the evidence supports the CRI assessment.
processes.name: Execute disaster recovery test

processes.description: Design, register, and operate an interface between systems. Integration onboarding registers the interface, its data, and its owners before traffic flows; unregistered interfaces are how impact analysis goes blind.
processes.name: Onboard and operate integration

processes.description: Configure platform, product, treatment, and reporting for a new client program. Program configuration translates the client contract into platform, product, treatment, and reporting settings; every setting traces to a contract clause or a documented default.
processes.name: Configure client program

processes.description: Migrate a client portfolio onto the servicing platform with reconciled balances and no cardholder disruption.
processes.name: Convert client portfolio

processes.description: Migrate a client portfolio off the servicing platform and hand over records. Deconversion hands a portfolio off with data, documents, and cutover timing per contract; the obligation to do it well survives the relationship ending.
processes.name: Deconvert client portfolio

processes.description: Produce and deliver reporting to the schedule and specification in the client contract. Contracted reporting ships to specification and schedule; late or wrong reporting is an SLA breach with credits, so production is monitored like any critical batch.
processes.name: Produce contracted client reporting

processes.description: Send and receive contracted data feeds with the client on schedule. Data feeds run both directions on contracted schedules with schema and quality checks at the boundary; feed failures page, because clients reconcile against them.
processes.name: Exchange client data feed

processes.description: Calculate and invoice servicing fees per the contract and recognize the revenue. Fee billing calculates from contracted schedules against actual volumes; invoices carry the detail clients audit, and revenue recognition follows the contract.
processes.name: Bill client servicing fees

work_packages.description: Stand up the installment lending product on the AWS landing zone: the edge and load balancer, the web and API tiers, the database, the object store, the async worker and the integration hub that fronts the ledger, the bureau and the CRM.
work_packages.name: Build installment lending on AWS
work_packages.notes: Ends a quarter before the product launch date so there is a quarter of parallel running against the card estate.

work_packages.description: Buy sanctions and adverse-media screening rather than build it: the vendor tenant, the integration gateway, the private egress path and the identity federation, plus the change to the authorization switch that calls it.
work_packages.name: Onboard the screening vendor
work_packages.notes: The only work package that changes a live system rather than only building new ones, which is why the switch appears with effect Changes.

work_packages.description: Replace the spreadsheet-based return with an engine sourcing from the warehouse, and extend the customer semantic layer with the fields the return needs.
work_packages.name: Stand up the regulatory reporting engine
work_packages.notes: Agreed and funded, not started, which is what Planned means here and what Active means on the two above it.

work_packages.description: Buy document and liveness verification rather than build it: the vendor tenancy, the gateway, the private path to the vendor, and the webhook listener that hands results back to the identity service.
work_packages.name: Onboard the identity verification vendor
work_packages.notes: The second vendor onboarding, and the first on the Azure landing zone over a private path.

work_packages.description: The first product on the Azure digital shape: the catalog and redemption web front end and API, the product datastore, the event publisher, and the worker that fulfills a redemption after the response. Balances stay with the proposed rewards ledger; this is the channel in front of it.
work_packages.name: Build rewards redemption on Azure
work_packages.notes: Five new systems and nothing live touched. The worker asked the Azure landing zone for an event stream it did not have; Event Hubs was added to the landing zone for this package, which is the only thing about it that is not a shape and a handful of answers.

work_packages.description: The merchant portal from the library's parts: the API, the web channel, the datastore, the event publisher, and the onboarding analyst role the product creates. Assembled as one product file with no shape; the landing zone answers for the gateway, the cluster, the database and the bus.
work_packages.name: Assemble the merchant portal on Azure
work_packages.notes: Four new systems and a role, nothing live touched. The first project assembled from parts; its compose block is the whole architecture.

work_packages.description: The first product on the Google Cloud landing zone: the API, the web channel, the datastore and the event publisher of the digital shape, resolved against GKE, Apigee, Cloud SQL and Pub/Sub. The dealer integrations that start an application already run through Apigee, so the product lands beside its partners.
work_packages.name: Land point-of-sale finance on Google Cloud
work_packages.notes: Four new systems on a third cloud, nothing live touched. The landing zone is nineteen services the zone owners stand up once; the product is a handful of answers on the shape.

work_packages.description: Open banking affordability from TrueLayer, reached over Private Service Connect from the lending project on Google Cloud and returning its assessment by webhook: the vendor shape's private path and webhook return, resolved against Google Cloud for the first time. Our side is a gateway, an egress and a listener beside the point-of-sale API.
work_packages.name: Buy affordability data for point-of-sale finance
work_packages.notes: Three systems of ours and the vendor's, all new; nothing live touched. The long-lead item is the private path, which the zone's Private Service Connect already provides.

work_packages.description: The first data product on the Google Cloud side: point-of-sale finance's events curated nightly into BigQuery in an analytics project of its own, served through Looker and registered in Collibra. The second workload project on the hub, so the product's tenancy and its analytics tenancy are separate.
work_packages.name: Curate lending performance in BigQuery
work_packages.notes: Two systems of ours, a dataset and a project; nothing live touched. The source is the product's own event publisher, so the pipeline waits on point-of-sale finance going live.
